{"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"reflow2 is consumable as a pinned, versioned container image, so a consumer needs no Rust toolchain and reflow2 needs no knowledge of their deploy","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"Raised by @ajs from flo2, 2026-08-05. flo2 wants to consume reflow2 as a pinned image rather than installing it, so that nobody building the web app needs a Rust toolchain and nobody maintaining reflow2 touches flo2's deploy. It is what lets a second contributor (@alex) consume reflow2 without building it.

THE JOB ITSELF IS SMALL AND IS NOT NEW MACHINERY. release.yml already builds a per-platform binary matrix (linux-x86_64, macos-arm64, macos-x86_64) and packages the consumer kit; a container is one more job in that workflow. Build for linux/amd64, and linux/arm64 too if flo2 may land on arm hosts. Tag the image with the reflow2 version already in [workspace.package], so a consumer pins a version rather than chasing latest. Publish to a registry flo2 can pull from. Run as a non-root user, and make sure the mounted data volume is writable by that uid — the commonest way a first container run fails. There is no Dockerfile in the repo today, so this starts from nothing.

TWO RUNTIME SETTINGS A SERVER NEEDS AND A LAPTOP DOES NOT. (1) The idle timeout does not belong on a hosted server: --idle-timeout defaults to 120 minutes and exists, per its own comment, because holding the lock blocks every CLI use of the graph — right for a developer's machine, wrong for a service, where the container exiting on idle looks like a crash loop to an orchestrator. The timeout is carried by the shared-server path, and the explicit --http branch constructs its surface with no SharedServer attached, so it appears not to apply there; which mode the container runs must be confirmed and the behaviour pinned rather than inherited. (2) Binding and reachability: the container must bind a routable address rather than loopback, and --http-allow-host is DNS-rebinding protection, NOT authentication. The image must be deployed on a private network behind flo2's gateway, and that expectation belongs in the image's own documentation so nobody deploys it thinking it defends itself.

READINESS. The rendezvous sidecar is written only AFTER the store is held and the port is bound, which makes it an honest readiness signal: if it exists, the server got all the way up. A healthcheck can use that, or an equivalent endpoint. What a healthcheck must NOT do is report ready before a cold open finishes — opening a large design builds its full-text index and takes seconds, not milliseconds.","status":"accepted"}
